newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian city has mini-sax for Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Belgian city has mini-sax for Clinton.

text.p: The Belgian city of Dinant, one-time home to Adolphe Sax the inventor of the saxophone, will on Monday hand U.S. officials a gold brooch replica of the instrument as a gift for President Bill Clinton.
Clinton, whose busy schedule forced him to pass up an invitation to visit the city when he was in Belgium two years ago, is a keen amateur saxophonist.

The 5.5 cm high brooch made of solid 18 carat yellow and white gold is the work of Scottish bagpiper-turned-jeweller Iain Wood who has lived in Belgium since 1976 and in Dinant for the past six months.
"I used to live in Namur where the city symbol is a snail, so I used to make hundreds of gold snails," he told Reuters by telephone from his shop, "Wood-MacArthur".
"But when I moved to Dinant there was not much demand for snails, so I started making saxophone brooches instead," the 49-year-old former Scots Guardsman said.
Eager to make up for missing out on Clinton last time, the city fathers turned to Wood and asked him to make a saxophone brooch specially for the U.S. president.
Wood said the Clinton brooch, an exact replica of Adolphe Sax's original instrument, would have a retail value of about 70,000 francs ($2,300).
